1. The strongest construction I developed

I selected four retractable steel capture heads with independent preload springs and positive mechanical retention.

The intended improvement over the earlier copper and solder constructions is substantial at the operational level: readiness no longer depends on reproducing a deposited seam, relocating a molten alloy, reversing electrode morphology or restoring a clean chemical interface. The structural material remains in identifiable solid parts. Release first removes contact pressure, then moves those parts.

That does not make the latch principle new. ModLock already demonstrated rapid mechanical connection using prepared receiver patterns, and HiGen already combined extending, rotating and retracting mechanical elements with single-sided disconnection. Those inventions deserve credit. My proposed contribution was a particular recessed packaging, controlled unload-before-slide trajectory and observation arrangement; I have not established that this combination earns the requested advantage. 
modlabupenn.org
+1

Application and access

The declared application is an indoor, quasistatic equipment or inspection-fixture mount:

Normal robot approach.
Access to a drive port behind the active carrier.
Temporary access around the carrier for a support/proof tool.
No human occupancy, impact loading, applied torsion or sustained vibration.
All permanent parts remain inside 49 × 49 mm.
The application permits up to 2 mm mating-feature projection, so a competent screw/key alternative is not excluded simply because the proposed heads retract completely.

The proposed assembly is 30.6 mm deep across both halves. It is therefore a recessed connector, not an ultrathin adhesive interface.

The useful wrench is defined at the center of the mating plane. External lever arms must be transformed to that plane. For example, 1,000 N applied 20 mm away creates 20 N·m and is outside the reference envelope.

I separately allowed a conservative 4.9 N self-force and 0.1 N·m self-moment for a 0.5 kg joint allowance. Finished mass and center of gravity would have to replace that allowance.
